=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:3748-3749,5491-5492 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Both late-Implement cancel lookups read only one page of implement.yml runs (`per_page=100` in "Cleanup test artifacts", `per_page=20` in "Cleanup alt-model artifacts") and filter by title and active status afterwards, so a matching stuck run that falls past that page is never cancelled.
  WHY: The uncancelled run can open the late ai/issue-<N> PR after cleanup, and only the sweep backstop catches it (up to SWEEP_SMOKE_PR_MAX_AGE_HOURS later); Phase 3b already pages the same window, and the workflow itself documents a run lost to truncation (line 1092, index 96; lines 833-836). Severity disagrees: openai_gpt-6-luna says MAJOR, while anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash say NIT; the highest is used.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:3756,5469 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup steps for late Implement runs use a fixed page size (per_page=100 or 20) when listing workflow runs.
  WHY: If the matching active run is past the returned page, it is not cancelled and can open the late PR this change is meant to prevent. This is the same root cause as the entry above, but the cited lines fall outside the 5-line merge window, so it is listed separately.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4865-4876 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `for attempt in 1 2 3` branch-delete loop treats a 404 for a never-created `orchestrator/project-<N>` branch as a transient failure: it retries with 2 s and 4 s sleeps, then emits `::warning::Could not delete branch ${PROJECT_BRANCH} after 3 attempts`.
  WHY: Every release run where the branch is absent wastes about 6 s and gets a misleading warning annotation; the step still exits 0, so correctness is not affected.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:34047-34048 | severity=high | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The new `judge_tracking_issue_closed_skip wave-advance` call adds a tracking-issue GET (get_issue_state_labels_json, lines 4813-4817) to every in_progress verdict with NEW_ISSUES_COUNT=0, and the checks tests-hooks-and-orchestrator and orchestrate-poll (2) fail on head 441d75a.
  WHY: The CI failure has not been attributed: a harness fixture whose tracking issue is closed would now stop before the wave advance, and a test counting issue reads per tick would see one more. The required lint gate stays red until the failure is traced to this hunk or to an inherited cause.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:required gates on PR head 441d75a32cd2adf1e62e30e65ae59d2144da3e3a (run 42852534125; check-runs `lint`, `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, `orchestrate-poll (2)`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Three required gates fail on the current head, and the log tails do not name the failing test or step. The `lint_pr_body_auto_close` annotations match the #2734 postmortem fixture, not this PR's body, and the orchestrate-poll tail shows an integration-fingerprint error for #2523 / scripts/render_prompt.sh.
  WHY: The PR cannot pass its required `lint` aggregation gate, and without the failing step name nobody can confirm whether the failures are inherited or caused by the judge-guard changes. The earlier claim that the selector change fixed the lint failure is contradicted by the 16:28 re-run.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10276-10282 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The function header comment says the guard does "one GET, only when the judge proposed new issues", but the same run adds a `type=wave-advance` call (line 34048) that reads the state exactly when `NEW_ISSUES_COUNT -eq 0`.
  WHY: This is comment drift, not a runtime failure, but it misstates the at-most-one-read-per-arm contract that the API-call budget depends on.

  WHY: About 6 s wasted and a misleading warning on each such release run; the step still exits 0.
